questions.title: The somatic motor pathway is a single-neuron system
questions.question: Regarding the somatic nervous system, which of the following is correct?

options.A: It controls the functions of skeletal muscle
options.B: Its effect is rapid and intense
options.C: It controls the functions of plain muscle, exocrine glands and cardiac muscle

explanations.A: Correct. The somatic motor pathway from the spinal cord to skeletal muscle is a single-neuron (one-neuron) system, in contrast to the two-neuron (preganglionic then postganglionic) autonomic efferent pathway; its effector organ is specifically skeletal muscle, which it controls under voluntary command. This single-neuron arrangement, with no intervening ganglion, is part of why somatic reflexes and voluntary movements are faster than autonomic responses to the same stimulus. The autonomic system's extra synaptic relay, by contrast, buys it the ability to modulate its output pharmacologically at the ganglion, a site the somatic pathway has no equivalent of.
explanations.B: Incorrect. While somatic conduction is fast, describing the effect simply as "rapid and intense" does not capture what distinguishes the somatic system -- its defining feature tested here is the single-neuron pathway to skeletal muscle, not a vague speed/intensity claim.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Control of plain (smooth) muscle, exocrine glands and cardiac muscle is the autonomic nervous system's job, not the somatic system's, which is restricted to skeletal muscle.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The somatic nervous system controls voluntary, not involuntary, actions; involuntary control of visceral effectors is the autonomic nervous system's role.

questions.learning_objective: Contrast the single-neuron somatic motor pathway to skeletal muscle with the two-neuron autonomic efferent pathway.
